# Methods: outpatient_visits

_Each sentence below is the decision record's own, as it stood when this bundle was exported: answers changed before anything was seen are folded out, every change made after the held-out rows were opened is kept and marked, a sentence that counts rows counts them as they stand, and confirmations alike but for their column are said once, together. Sections follow TRIPOD+AI; a paragraph that is not the record's was written by the analysis on these answers._

## Data (TRIPOD+AI 5)

The table was read through the `clinical` lens.

## Participants (TRIPOD+AI 6)

No rows were excluded: every row with `admitted_2y` measured stays in the analysis.

`sex` was recoded with `f` as `1` and `m` as `0`.

`admitted_2y` was chosen as the outcome; it is measured on all `1,600` rows. `1` of `admitted_2y` was taken as the event and coded 1; `0` was coded 0. `admitted_2y` was analyzed as a yes/no outcome: everyone was followed for the same time, as answered, so it counts events over one period.

## Predictors (TRIPOD+AI 9)

Column roles were set for `16` columns: predictors `clinic`, `age`, `sex` and 12 more; identifier `patient_id`. `clinic` was confirmed as a measure on its own, after the evidence for its proposal was read. The 5 columns `waist_cm`, `sbp` and 3 more, proposed as characteristics at medium confidence, below high, for one reason ("A person's characteristic."), were confirmed together as one group, after the evidence for their proposal was read. The 4 columns `ldl`, `hdl` and 2 more, proposed as measures at low confidence, below high, for one reason ("A measured column: read as a predictor until you say otherwise."), were confirmed together as one group, after the evidence for their proposal was read. The 2 columns `drinks_per_week` and `steps_per_day`, proposed as measures at low confidence, below high, for one reason ("An amount per day or week: a rate, read as a predictor for now."), were confirmed together as one group, after the evidence for their proposal was read. `steps_per_day`, `ldl`, `sbp`, `hdl`, `age`, `dbp` and `drinks_per_week` were each confirmed to hold amounts or counts, on its own, after the evidence for its reading was read.

Read from the values, no question asked: `patient_id` is the unit's identifier (Named like a participant's identifier; `1,600` labels, one per row); `age` is a characteristic (A person's characteristic); `sex` is a characteristic (A person's characteristic); `bmi` is a characteristic (A person's characteristic); `admitted_2y` is a binary outcome (Only `0` and `1` — read as a binary outcome); `bmi` is an amount (one slope) (`246` values with decimals that fill their grid as a measurement's do (a code list's sit apart)); `waist_cm` is an amount (one slope) (`538` values with decimals that fill their grid as a measurement's do (a code list's sit apart)); `hba1c` is an amount (one slope) (`29` values with decimals that fill their grid as a measurement's do (a code list's sit apart)); `sleep_hours` is an amount (one slope) (`67` values with decimals that fill their grid as a measurement's do (a code list's sit apart)); `clinic` holds codes for categories (one indicator per label) (`3` labels, not numbers); `smoking` holds codes for categories (one indicator per label) (`3` labels, not numbers); `education` holds codes for categories (one indicator per label) (`4` labels, not numbers).

## Missing data (TRIPOD+AI 11)

Missing predictor values were imputed in each training fold without the outcome: the median for numbers, the most frequent value for categories; no row was dropped for a missing predictor.

## Analytical methods (TRIPOD+AI 12)

The analysis was declared for `prediction`: models are judged on rows they never saw. A random `20%` of the rows with `admitted_2y` recorded (seed `0`, stratified by `admitted_2y`) was held out for one final score; performance was estimated on the rest by `5`-fold cross-validation; the optimism of each model's apparent performance was estimated by Harrell's bootstrap (`500` resamples, the whole pipeline refit on each) and subtracted, except for a family that nearly memorizes its rows (boosted trees), whose cross-validated score stands because the bootstrap overstates it; models were compared with each other and with the no-predictor baseline on `5`-fold cross-validation repeated `10` times, by the corrected repeated k-fold t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004). Two model families were chosen: elastic net and screened elastic net.

Within each training fold, sure independence screening were fitted and applied to the held-out fold; elastic-net parameters were tuned by an inner CV within the rows each fit was given.

Cross-validated scores are the mean over folds; the fold values show the spread.

Each standard error counts which rows were scored, with each fold's model as fitted (LeDell et al. 2015; DeLong's for the AUC); it leaves out how the models would vary with other training rows.

With elastic net declared the final model on cross-validation beforehand, the `320` held-out rows were opened once and scored: held-out log loss `0.487` (AUC `0.5`, the customary headline); its held-out score is the reported result, the other families' are secondary, and any later change is marked as made after the seal was opened.

## Other decisions

The open noticings were triaged in Results: 1 left as a limitation.

## Reproducibility

The analysis was run in TurboTab 2.0.0.dev0 (source revision `4c5db134f399`, with local changes). The supplementary provenance record holds the decision log (`24` records), the SHA-256 of the input file `outpatient_visits.csv` (SHA-256 `e3b11600ffd1`), the analysis plan (SHA-256 `b6abfa04d3a2`) and the model matrix (`1,280` rows by `22` columns; SHA-256 `ac07e96c5607` as Parquet). Replaying it with `python -m turbotab.replay` checks each input file against its hash and refuses one that differs; otherwise it rebuilds the analysis from the input files and the decision log alone and compares the model matrix and every reported estimate with these.
